hook: A river carries too much nitrogen to the sea. Regulators can find the sewage plant's outfall pipe on a map, measure what comes out of it and set a limit. But three quarters of the nitrogen enters from somewhere else: from thousands of fields, lawns and streets every time it rains. There is no pipe to point at.

options: Water that flows over the land surface into streams
Water that soaks into an aquifer
prereq.why: Runoff flows over the surface and carries what it picks up into streams.

options: All the land that drains into one river or lake
A layer of rock that holds groundwater
prereq.why: Everything that happens on the land in a watershed can reach its river.

figure.caption: Point sources enter at one place you can find; nonpoint sources wash in from across the whole watershed.

chain.cause: A factory or sewage plant releases waste through one pipe or stack
chain.effect: it is a point source that can be found, measured and given a permit

chain.cause: Rain falls on fields, lawns, streets and construction sites across a watershed
chain.effect: runoff picks up fertilizer, sediment, oil, metals and pet waste from many places

chain.cause: That runoff enters streams along their whole length
chain.effect: it is nonpoint pollution, with no single place to measure or treat

chain.cause: Laws have cut point sources sharply
chain.effect: nonpoint sources are now the largest share of water pollution and need land-use solutions

ideas: A point source comes from one identifiable place: a discharge pipe, a smokestack, a leaking tank or an oil tanker.
A nonpoint source comes from many diffuse places: runoff from farms, lawns and streets, eroded sediment, and car exhaust across a city.
Point sources are easier to measure, permit and treat, so laws such as the Clean Water Act have cut them a lot. Nonpoint sources now cause most water pollution.
Nonpoint fixes work on the land: buffer strips, rain gardens, permeable pavement, careful fertilizer use and erosion control.

misconception.wrong: The worst source of pollution is the one with the biggest pipe.
misconception.right: For many rivers and lakes, most pollution comes from nonpoint sources, such as runoff from thousands of fields and streets, which no single pipe carries.

summary: Point sources release pollution from one identifiable place, such as a pipe or smokestack, so they can be measured, permitted and treated. Nonpoint sources, such as runoff from farms, lawns and streets, come from many diffuse places. Laws have cut point sources sharply, so nonpoint pollution is now the largest share, and it is reduced by changing how land is used.
